body:
Fixes CITATION.cff name-particle leak across the org. Per the CFF spec, name-particle is for surname infixes (de/van/von) — not initials. Merges "P." into given-names as "Stephen P." and adds canonical email stephen@szlholdings.com.

Part of the Series-A doctrine cleanup (see audit report).
title: doctrine(citation): merge P. into given-names; add email

## Summary

Doctrine pre-release sweep found 4 of 5 hosted anatomy PDFs had stale or non-canonical Author metadata:
- `agent_architecture.pdf` → was 'Stephen P. Lutar Jr. / SZL Holdings'
- `brain.pdf` → was 'anonymous'
- `wires.pdf` → was 'anonymous'
- `hatun_body_graph.pdf` → was 'Perplexity Computer'

All four are replaced with doctrine-clean local copies (Author='Lutar, Stephen P.', zero forbidden strings — verified by pdftotext + grep).

Also adds PNG renditions of each so the figures can be embedded inline in email and web contexts without forcing PDF download.

## Verification
```
for f in anatomy/*.pdf; do python -c "from pypdf import PdfReader; r=PdfReader('$f'); print(r.metadata.get('/Author'))"; done
```
All print: `Lutar, Stephen P.`

```
for f in anatomy/*.pdf; do pdftotext "$f" - | grep -E 'Jr\.|Glass Wing|Pillpintu|Khipu|AlloyScape|Perplexity Computer' && echo FAIL || echo CLEAN; done
```
All print: `CLEAN`

Refs: doctrine pre-release sweep (zero generational suffix in any artifact)
title: docs(anatomy): doctrine fix — author metadata + PNG previews
